findings.description: ADR 0115's 2026-11-17 amendment says `+`, `@` and `!` join the refused characters and that `@scope` package paths must be named outside a rescope; the change now accepts a bare `+` or `@`.
findings.body:
**The change contradicts ADR 0115's 2026-11-17 amendment, and the PR doesn't update it.**

What the amendment says:
- Lines 256-261: "`(`, `)`, `|`, `+`, `@` and `!` join the refused metacharacters".
- A project with `@scope` package directories "names them outside a rescope".
- Line 269: "the refusal table takes each extglob character alone".

What the code at this head does: the metacharacter check is now `/[[\]{}\\()|!]/`. A bare `+` or `@` passes, and the new plain-path test asserts that `packages/@acme/ui/**` and `src/routes/+page.svelte` are accepted. The `@scope` sentence now says the opposite of what the code does.

AGENTS.md says ADRs win over the design docs where they conflict, so a reader will trust this text over the code. The amendment also doesn't record the two other changes in this PR:
- the new leading-`:` (git pathspec magic) refusal;
- the empty, absolute and `.`/empty-segment refusals now sharing one message.

Suggested fix: add an amendment, in the style of the earlier ones, saying:
- `(`, `)`, `|` and `!` stay refused, `!` anywhere in the glob;
- a bare `+` or `@` is literal, because extglob syntax needs a following `(`, which is refused;
- a leading `:` is refused;
- empty, absolute and `.`/empty-segment globs share one refusal.

Then correct the `@scope` sentence and the *Tests* sentence to match.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6977aceb412a151f0b8e711d8a08c35dfa93c83a/docs/adr/0115-pup-plan-edit-rescope-lets-the-operator-widen.md#L256-L271

findings.description: The new `globToRegExp` bare-`+` test sits in task-rescope.test.ts, but `globToRegExp` has its own sibling suite, src/core/glob-utils.test.ts, which already holds the 'escapes regex specials' case.
The 'Git pathspec magic' comment sits above one row (`:^src`), but the unrelated `'  '` and `'./'` rows follow it with no comment of their own, so they read as part of that group.
